tool.excerpt: Flávio Bolsonaro Beats Lula in First Round; Runoff Set for October 25 CubaHeadlines Flávio Bolsonaro Beats Lula in First Round; Runoff Set for October 25 Monday, October 5, 2026 by Henry Cruz Flávio Bolsonaro and Luis Ignacio “Lula” da Silva - Image of © Wikipedia In a surprising turn of events, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro emerged victorious over President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the initial round of Brazil's presidential elections. According to the official results from the Superior Electoral Court, Bolsonaro secured 47.06% of the valid votes, while Lula garnered 45.13%, with 99.88% of the votes counted. The margin between the two candidates was approximately 2.3 million votes — 56,075,582 for Bolsonaro compared to 53,778,788 for Lula — falling short of the 50% threshold required for an outright win. Consequently, both candidates will face off in a runoff election on October 25. A Resilient Comeback for Flávio Bolsonaro This outcome marks a significant achievement for the 45-year-old Flávio Bolsonaro , who initially was perceived as a weak contender and is currently under investigation for corruption. As the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro —who is serving house arrest after being sentenced to 27 years for leading a coup plot—Flávio was appointed as the Liberal Party's (PL) candidate by his father from prison in December 2025. Meanwhile, the 80-year-old Lula is aiming for an unprecedented fourth term. However, the outlook for the runoff appears grim for him, as he ran as the sole candidate from the progressive side, which limits his ability to rally additional support. In contrast, Bolsonaro is expected to secure the backing of eliminated right-wing candidates, who collectively hold around 7% of the vote. Political Shifts and Implications Political analyst Creomar de Souza expressed skepticism about Lula's chances in the second round, highlighting the historical difficulty of overcoming a deficit in a Brazilian runoff. "Historically, a comeback in a second-round election has never happened in Brazil. It's a very challenging scenario for Lula," he told the BBC. De Souza also noted the effectiveness of Flávio's campaign, particularly in the last week, in framing the election as an effort to unseat Lula rather than focusing on Flávio himself.
